title: Strelley Pool stromatolite reef, Pilbara
summary: In the Pilbara of Western Australia, the Strelley Pool Chert preserves a multi-kilometre field of layered stromatolites about 3.43 billion years old, which the discoverers read as a reef built by microbes in shallow seas. It is among the oldest large records of apparent life, though biogenicity of such rocks is debated.

uncertainty.note: Allwood et al. (2006) give 3,430 Ma; Duda et al. (2016) give the formation as 3.43-3.35 Ga; the inHerit record says approximately 3420 million years. Uncertainty is a rounding bracket.

where.modern_name: Strelley Pool area, East Pilbara, Western Australia (sampling section on the Shaw River; about 34 km west of Marble Bar)
where.historical_name: Shallow marine carbonate platform on the Pilbara Craton (no human geography)

paleo.not_applicable: MERDITH2021 covers only 0-1000 Ma and PALEOMAP 0-750 Ma; no GPlates model in the tool reaches 3,430 Ma.

importance.justification: One of the oldest widely cited records of microbial reef-building, bearing on how early and how diverse life was.

reviewer_note: The pin is the Duda et al. sampling section on the other side of the Shaw River from the Trendall locality, not the exact type locality; the reef extends over more than 10 km of outcrop (Allwood). Biological origin is debated, and the summary reflects that. No GPlates model reaches 3.43 Ga.
